name: Unicode multilingual character standard
description: A shared code for representing multilingual text across computer systems and applications.

impact.note: Nearly all text on phones and computers is encoded with it; it unified existing character codes, with a few direct extensions resting on it.

date.label: October 1990
date.basis: Unicode Consortium dates its publicly distributed preview to October 1990.

events.statement: The Unicode Consortium distributed an early Unicode preview for public review.
events.caveats: This draft contained initial code charts and mapping tables; it was not the released 1991 Unicode Standard. The source says it was fairly widely distributed but gives no user count.

evidence.supports: The Unicode history lists an October 1990 public preview with draft charts and mapping tables.

date.label: December 1990
date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: A Unicode 1.0 final-review draft was made public.
events.caveats: This was a draft, not a final published standard. An earlier October 1990 preview contained initial draft charts.

evidence.supports: The consortium lists a public final-review draft in December 1990.

date.label: October 1991
date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: The Unicode Consortium published the first version of the Unicode Standard.
events.caveats: Version 1.0 used a 16-bit scheme and did not include every language or script; later Unicode differs.

evidence.supports: Consortium dates the first version to October 1991.

earliest_record.rationale: The October 1990 preview is the earliest documented public distribution among the events; it was a draft, not the 1991 standard release.

caveats: Earlier national and international character codes preceded Unicode; formal encoding is not evidence that any particular community had fonts or software support.

research.note: Initial sourced research; independent review pending. Independent review identified the earlier October public preview and distinguishes it from the December final-review draft and 1991 version 1 release.
